newsitem.title: INDIA: India deputies seek lower taxes in 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: India deputies seek lower taxes in 1997/98 budget.

text.p: Indian lawmakers who form a core committee of parliamentary advisors to the finance ministry asked the government on Tuesday to substantially cut personal income tax in the 1997/98 budget, an official statement said.

The Consultative Committee of the Finance Ministry also urged Finance Miister P. Chidambaram to review the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) in the April-March budget he is due to present on February 28.
FERA is opposed by the industry as an archaic law which impedes India's efforts to introduce convertibility of the rupee on capital account.
The government says it wants to allow full convertibility of the rupee but has sought more time to implement the measure.

The lawmakers' body, whose advice is not binding on the ministry, sought the lower slab of income tax to be cut from 15 percent to 10 percent and the upper bracket to be lowered from 40 percent to 30 percent, the statement said.
The committee also asked Chidambaram to allow private competition in the state-owned insurance sector, the statement said.
